payload.explanation: Monitor slip_u_orange (authored, clause: in-hand slippage invariant, threshold 0.02m from raw_spec.tolerances.grasp_slip_tolerance_m) fired at trigger_wall_ns=1792197608910913500 with observed relative translation 0.0202m between u_orange and the gripper TCP, just over threshold. get_evidence over the surrounding window (object_poses for u_orange vs frames for tcp) shows the TCP's own orientation essentially constant (qx~0.7076, qy~0.7066, qz/qw near 0) while u_orange's orientation drifted steadily over the same ~1s window (quaternion y component 0.033->0.070, z component 0.030->0.079), with its position also shifting a few mm in x/y beyond the gripper's motion. This is not sensor noise or a timing artifact (tcp and object samples are time-paired) -- the object is physically rotating/pivoting inside the gripper while being lowered into place_u_orange, consistent with the part catching an edge (likely against u_brown or the base1 slot) during insertion rather than a clean seat. This violates the in-hand slippage invariant (object must not move relative to the gripper before release). End-state seating will still be checked independently at this step's close and at the final run verdict to determine whether the part nonetheless landed within its placement tolerance.

payload.explanation:
This is the run's final end-state verdict, covering all 12 steps observed. All 12 steps matched the expected process map; no unplanned step_id occurred (u_orange's reseat happened under the same step_id place_u_orange, not a new begin_step). Throughout the run I kept standing authored monitors on: the five bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) and base1 for disturbance (threshold 0.02m, raw_spec.tolerances.disturbance_tolerance_m), each of this task's four parts for disturbance whenever inactive, held-object-gated clamp-effort monitors for all four parts (thresholds from raw_spec.limits.max_clamp_effort: 100/200/170/250), and in-hand-slippage monitors (tol 0.02m, raw_spec.tolerances.grasp_slip_tolerance_m) during each part's carry. None of the bystander or base1 monitors ever fired across the whole run, and I additionally confirmed base1 and all five bystanders' final poses were consistent with their rest poses via query_snapshot at each milestone -- the fixture and other assembly's parts were never disturbed.

One real finding occurred: at place_u_orange, the slip_u_orange monitor fired (observed 0.0202m vs 0.02m threshold). get_evidence around the fire showed u_orange's orientation rotating steadily in the gripper while the TCP's own orientation stayed essentially fixed -- a genuine physical slip (the part catching an edge during insertion), not sensor noise. I recorded this as non_conformant under place_u_orange at the time. The executor's own end_step report for place_u_orange corroborated it independently: it measured a 28.3deg orientation error on the first placement, re-grasped u_orange at its settled pose, and reseated it. I independently re-queried u_orange's pose after the correction and measured 0.00208m from u_orange_placement (threshold 0.02m) and negligible orientation error -- within tolerance. u_brown's disturbance during this rework measured 0.0033m via my own snapshot, also within its 0.02m tolerance. This is a recovery: a mid-run violation that was corrected before the step closed.

For the final end-state I independently queried every part's placement frame and its own pose via query_snapshot (not the executor's claims): u_brown 0.00213m/≈0deg (tol 0.01m/10deg), u_orange 0.00209m/≈0.3deg (tol 0.02m/10deg) after correction, line_green 0.00656m/≈0.2deg (tol 0.015m/10deg), inverted_u_yellow 0.00257m/≈1.1-1.9deg (tol 0.012m/10deg) -- all four parts are seated within their placement tolerances at run end, and cross-checking each part's pose at every subsequent milestone showed no part was disturbed again after being seated. Grasp effects (lift height >=0.05m, grasp width error <=0.02m band, effort plateau >=0.05 floor) were satisfied for every part at its own place step using the grasped-phase event data (or, for u_orange's second/corrected grasp, the lift skill's own height parameter and the fact that the slip monitor armed fresh for that attempt never fired, which is also the direct evidence for the object_tcp_offset_m clauses given object_tcp_offset_m and grasp_slip_tolerance_m share the same 0.02m-or-tighter bound for these parts and no monitor crossed it on any attempt). Instantaneous clamp effort never approached any part's limit (observed 21-29 against limits of 100-250). No unidentified object ever appeared in the workspace in any of my looks (baseline and final), and a final camera look confirms the scene matches expectations with all four target parts seated and all five bystanders undisturbed in their original positions.

Given one violation was found and subsequently corrected before its step closed, and every part's end-state measured by me independently is within tolerance with no violation standing at run end, the run's end-state is conformant (recovered).
